part.text: The field supports annual totals by summing pedestrian fatalities across crashes. The dataset has records through 2025; I’m producing two standard views of the same annual counts—a bar chart for year-by-year comparison and a line chart for the time trend.

input.command: python3 -c "import duckdb, pandas as pd, matplotlib.pyplot as plt; from pathlib import Path; out=Path('out'); df=duckdb.query(\"SELECT year(crash_date) AS year, CAST(sum(number_of_pedestrians_killed) AS BIGINT) AS pedestrian_deaths FROM read_parquet('data/crashes.parquet') WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01' AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1\").df(); years=pd.DataFrame({'year': range(2013,2026)}); df=years.merge(df,on='year',how='left').fillna({'pedestrian_deaths':0}); df['pedestrian_deaths']=df['pedestrian_deaths'].astype(int); df.to_csv(out/'values_1.csv',index=False); df.to_csv(out/'values_2.csv',index=False); plt.figure(figsize=(10,5.5)); plt.bar(df.year.astype(str),df.pedestrian_deaths,color='#4776A8'); plt.title('Pedestrians killed in NYC motor vehicle crashes, 2013–2025'); plt.xlabel('Year'); plt.ylabel('Pedestrians killed'); plt.ylim(0,200); plt.grid(axis='y',alpha=.25); plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig(out/'option_1.png',dpi=160); plt.close(); plt.figure(figsize=(10,5.5)); plt.plot(df.year,df.pedestrian_deaths,marker='o',linewidth=2,color='#4776A8'); plt.title('Pedestrians killed in NYC motor vehicle crashes, 2013–2025'); plt.xlabel('Year'); plt.ylabel('Pedestrians killed'); plt.xticks(df.year); plt.ylim(0,200); plt.grid(axis='both',alpha=.25); plt.tight_layout(); plt.savefig(out/'option_2.png',dpi=160); plt.close(); print(df.to_string(index=False))"
